parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing exposure is documented: gender identity is not criminalised (2020 penal code), the old colonial provision was repealed, and no universal-exposure measure (facility bans, document screening, custody mandate, care denial) appears in the record. Positives carry weight: functioning courts struck down the 'moral order' clause (2017), Articles 191/160 provide on-paper protection with gender identity as an aggravating factor, a March 2026 source records broadly neutral societal attitudes, 85% of surveyed respondents opposed LGBTQ violence, and the only dated violence assessment (2015) reports no targeting. Deterrents are mostly resident-facing (no LGR, no service anti-discrimination) and do not reach the visitor. What holds this below the 0.80s: open questions on border document treatment, custody placement and facilities; penal provisions with no recorded prosecutions (paper protection, tier 5); no documented service protections operating for travelers; and trans-specific social acceptance unevidenced (surveys are LGB-framed, dated to 2017).
